Should flag

A closing paragraph of the previous block of content, sitting directly above the crowded heading with no gap at all.

Flag Crowded One

The content this heading introduces sits forty pixels away while the previous block touches the heading.

Another closing paragraph of a previous content block, again flush against the heading that follows it in the flow.

Flag Crowded Two

Second crowded case. Two or more headings must violate the principle before the rule fires on a page.

A third closing paragraph that the next heading will visually attach to, which is the inversion this rule measures.

Flag Crowded Three

Third crowded case, this time an h3, to confirm the rule reads h2 through h4 and not only the top level.

A paragraph of running prose, set with one uniform margin, so the subhead below sits as close to it as to its own text.

Flag Near Equal Under Prose

Twenty pixels above and twenty-four below, under two lines of body copy: the subhead reads as part of the run above.

Another paragraph of running prose. The subhead below keeps exactly the gap it keeps to the paragraph it introduces.

Flag Even Under Prose

Twenty-four pixels on both sides of the subhead, under body copy that runs across the column.

A closing paragraph ten pixels above a title whose module box is painted the same white as the page around it.

Flag White Module Title

The white fill shows no edge, so the paragraph above is still the title's neighbour.

A closing paragraph ten pixels above a title over a carousel that draws its slides in a shadow tree.

Flag Title Over Shadow Carousel

The next module starts well below the carousel; the title introduces the carousel, not this.

Flag Wrapped Section Title

Should pass

Pass First Heading

The first heading in its case has nothing above it, so it is exempt from the rhythm comparison entirely.

A paragraph with plenty of room after it. The heading below keeps sixty-four pixels above and sixteen below.

Pass Generous Above

Sixty-four pixels above and sixteen below. The heading clearly binds to this paragraph, the healthy shape.

A short line of copy.

Pass Even Under One Line

Even spacing under a single line is not running prose: a closing line, a kicker, a caption.

A paragraph before a heading whose spacing above and below is nearly equal, with more room above than the crowded test asks.

Pass More Room Above

Twenty-four pixels above and twenty below. The heading sits closer to its own content, the healthy direction.

A paragraph before an eyebrow label. The label belongs to the heading cluster, and the cluster has room above it.

Chapter Four

Pass Eyebrow Cluster

Space is measured from the top of the cluster, where seventy-two pixels separate it from the text above.

A paragraph before an eyebrow that a site builder wrapped in its own box, with the title wrapped in another box.

Introducing

Pass Eyebrow In Wrapper

The wrapped label is still the heading's own label, and seventy-two pixels separate the pair from the text above.

A block of content that ends in a rule. The rule is the section break, so the heading below starts a section.

Pass Divider Above

Twenty-four pixels to the rule above and forty-eight to this paragraph; the rule already separates the blocks.

A block of content followed by a horizontal rule, then a heading twelve pixels under that rule.

Pass Rule Above

The measured block above is the rule itself, which separates the sections rather than crowding the heading.

Pass Accordion Question That Opens The List

Pass Accordion Question In The Middle Row

Pass Accordion Question On The Last Row

Pass Caption Under Photo

A caption set tight under its own photo belongs to that photo. The gap below leads to the card's copy.

A block of content directly above a section title that draws a rule above and below its own text.

Pass Banded Title

The title band's own rule is the separator above it, so the zero gap to the block above is not crowding.

A paragraph twenty-four pixels above a heading whose standfirst sits behind a wrapper that generates no box at all.

Pass Standfirst Behind Contents

A short standfirst twelve pixels under the heading.

A paragraph before a small card. The card boundary provides the separation for the heading inside it.

Pass Card Heading

A heading inside a small card. The rule exempts headings inside panels shorter than two hundred pixels.

A paragraph before a banded section. The heading is the first content inside a section with its own background.

Pass Band Heading

This heading is the first content inside a section that draws its own background, so the band edge separates.

A paragraph that a pull quote follows without a gap, as an article sets a quotation into its running text.

Pass Pull Quote Heading

A heading set inside a quotation is the quotation set large. It heads no section, so its spacing sets no rhythm.

Wrapper spacing

A closing paragraph above a section header whose own padding holds sixteen pixels above the title.

Flag Header Padding

The header's forty-eight pixels of bottom padding sit between the title and this, the content it introduces.

A block editor wraps every text in a box. This one is the previous block, closing its content.

Flag Block Padding

The heading block's own padding holds the spacing: sixteen above the title, forty-eight below it.

A closing paragraph above a title wrapper with a few pixels of bottom padding and a margin under it.

Flag Small Padding

Six pixels of padding and forty-two of margin still put forty-eight pixels between the title and this.

A closing paragraph above a title set beside an icon that is taller than the title's own line.

Flag Icon Beside Heading

The icon stretches the row, and the row's margin puts this content well away from the title.

A closing paragraph above a pricing title row whose button is taller than the title.

Flag Tall Button Row

View all plans

The plans the title introduces start under the whole row, fifty-eight pixels below the title.

The left column closes with a paragraph and then a title.

Flag Column Heading

The right column holds a shorter paragraph.

What the column title introduces runs under the whole row, forty-eight pixels below the title.

A closing paragraph ten pixels above a heading whose gap below is an empty spacer box.

Flag Spacer Below

The spacer holds forty-eight pixels open between the heading and this content.

A builder's flex stack puts every text in a wrapper of its own and every gap in an empty box.

Flag Stack Heading

Sixteen pixels of spacer above the title, forty-eight below it before this content.

A closing paragraph, then a date line in a wrapper, set like the body copy rather than as a label.

Updated March 2026

Flag Plain Line Above

The date is content of its own, so the title sits ten pixels under it and forty-eight above this.

A closing paragraph, then a code block framed on every side, twelve pixels above the next heading.

npm install impeccable
npx impeccable detect src/

Flag Code Block Above

The frame is the code block's own box, not a rule, so the heading still sits closer to it than to this.

A builder puts every block in a layout row. This row closes the previous block's content.

Flag Title Alone In A Row

Feature One

The first column of the row the title introduces.

Feature Two

The second column of the row the title introduces.

A closing paragraph above a heading that ends a box drawing a rule under it.

Pass Heading Ends Ruled Box

The rule under the box ends the heading's box, so this content belongs to the next one.

A closing paragraph, then a news card whose grey section link sits a few pixels above its headline.

Política

Pass Grey Kicker

The grey link is the headline's label, so the cluster starts at the link, twenty-four pixels under the block above.

A closing paragraph, then an italic eyebrow at body size that opens the box holding a section title.

Five screens

Pass Italic Eyebrow

The italic line is the title's label, and the cluster sits forty-eight pixels under the block above.

A closing paragraph, then a hairline eyebrow at body size that opens the box holding a section title.

Compare plans

Pass Light Eyebrow

The weight sets the line apart from the copy around it, so it is read as the title's label.

A block of tiles closes with a blue link to the full list, laid out in the same box as the tiles.

View all essays

Flag Link Closing Block

The link ends the tiles above, so the title sits twelve pixels under it and forty above this.

A post excerpt closes with its grey date, and the next post's title follows twelve pixels under the date.

March 3, 2026

Flag Date Closing Post

The date belongs to the post above, so the title sits twelve pixels under it and forty above this.

A closing paragraph twelve pixels above a heading that carries a small icon as its own background image.

Flag Icon Heading

The icon decorates the heading and draws no edge above it, so the heading is measured as any other.

A closing paragraph twelve pixels above a title that draws a short accent bar under itself with a gradient.

Flag Accent Bar Heading

The bar sits under the title and draws nothing along its top, so the title is measured as any other.

A closing paragraph, then a grey sentence ten pixels above the next title, too long to read as a label.

Filed under politics and the week in review

Flag Grey Sentence Above

A sentence is content of its own whatever its colour, so the title sits ten pixels under it and forty-eight above this.

A closing paragraph directly above a band whose grey is a background image rather than a colour.

Pass Image Band Heading

The band's edge separates the title from the paragraph above, as a colour band's does.

A closing paragraph directly above a band painted with a small tiled texture instead of a colour.

Pass Tiled Band Heading

The tiled texture covers the band, and its edge separates the title from the paragraph above.
